questions.question: Atriopeptin (ANP) acts at _____.

suspectLines.text: ANP acts on the collecting duct. ANP is secreted by the atria in response to an increase in ECF volume. It decreases Na+ reabsorption in the late distal tubule and collecting ducts and causes natriuresis. ANP causes dilation of afferent arterioles and constriction of efferent arterioles, resulting in increased RBF and increased GFR.

questions.question: In a patient with metabolic acidosis, which of the following changes are seen?

suspectLines.text: K+ secretion into the renal tubules is decreased when H+ secretion is increased (intracellular buffering of H+). Thus in metabolic acidosis, there is decreased K+ excretion.
